caller.true: The patch renames, removes or reshapes something outward-facing -- a function another script imports, a printed word a caller parses, a JSON key, a pred a document cites, a path in settings -- and nothing in the patch shows every reader updated.

bands.known_wrong: THE RE-PROMPT IS READ AS THE LABEL, AND A PLANNER RE-PROMPTS FOR OTHER REASONS: a STATUS, a STAND DOWN and a next assignment are all prompts, so a worker that was working fine and got its next sub-issue reads `yes`. A worker that went on by itself after a long pause reads `no` although a person would have called it stuck. A session that exited reads as waiting forever, since its transcript never moves. Minutes are measured against the clock of the machine that asked and not against the kind's own durations, which nothing here has tallied

state.plan: the sub-issue's `## Plan` section, whole, as the body carries it. It is read at `campaign-claim take`, which runs `check` -- BEFORE ANY SPEC IS WRITTEN, which is the moment the miss happens: the author searches `spec/` by hand, and what they miss is a duplicate scenario or a skipped Spec that needed one
state.scenarios: every command `spec/commands.snapshot.json` lists, keyed s1..sN in snapshot order, each its verb and name, a newline, and the nearest `--` comment line above its declaration in the `checks.als` the snapshot names -- 215 of the 242 have one at 2026-09-18, and the count moves with `spec/`, and one whose declaration has none carries its name alone. THE HEADING IS SHARED: `-- the floor` sits above a run of commands and belongs to each of them, so the walk up passes another declaration and stops at a block comment, which is the module's own header and about no command. CUT BY ENTITY ONLY WHERE THE PLAN NAMES ONE, and a Plan naming none gets ALL OF THEM: that is the ordinary case and not a fallback. 133 of this tracker's 138 Plans name no entity at all (4 name a `spec/<entity>/...als` path, 1 a declared command in backticks), and the whole state, every command and an empty Plan, is 22,444 bytes against `STATE_BUDGET`'s 60,000 -- per entity the scenarios alone are orchestration 157 commands and 15,754 bytes, sdlc 33/2,523, github 24/2,253, session 18/1,138, directory 10/628, all at 2026-09-18. So NO STATE IS SKIPPED FOR WANT OF AN ENTITY, and the entity cut buys a narrower field where it is there to read and nothing where it is not. THE CEILING IS THE OPTION COUNT AND NOT THE BYTES: the endpoint takes `campaign-jev.py`'s `OPTION_BUDGET` options, 255, counting the entry's own `noMatch`, and refuses 256 with an HTTP 400 that reads exactly like an outage (measured by binary search, sdlc-alloy#458 S7). `spec/` declared 244 commands when this was measured and 242 two merges later, THIRTEEN UNDER IT, and the count moves both ways, so this is the branch the tree grows into: a cut at or over the ceiling is a SKIP ROW naming the count, never a field quietly shortened to fit, because a reading that stopped offering the right answer still answers. The word match that would guess one was measured and refused: `session`, `directory` and the rest are ordinary prose here -- a Claude session far more often than the spec entity -- so it would pick an entity off a coincidence (sdlc-alloy#458 NOTE 5724505059)
state.why: the duplicate is invisible at the moment it is made. `spec/` holds 242 commands over 5 entities at 2026-09-18 and nothing reads a Plan against them, so whether one already covers the behaviour is asked of whoever is about to write the Spec, by hand, and the state above is that search made once and recorded

prefilter.what: a sub-issue `campaign-tracker check` read that carries a `## Plan`; a campaign issue, a chore, and a sub-issue with no Plan ask nothing and are written as skip rows naming which rule took them. TWO MORE ARE SETTLED RATHER THAN ASKED, and code decides both: a Plan naming a snapshot command by its EXACT name in backticks is that command, passed as `settled` and never sent to the model -- the author already did the search this reading makes; and a tree with no snapshot, or one whose entity cut leaves no command, has nothing to pick from and is a skip row.
prefilter.entity: `campaign-tracker.py`'s `PLAN_ENTITY` and nowhere else. It is named and not restated here: this file held an ANCHORED copy of it, which matched no Plan line at all and so described a cut that never happens, and AGENTS.md refuses a second reader of a rule a script owns because the two drift exactly like that
prefilter.settled_by_name: a backticked span of the Plan whose text is the exact `name` of one snapshot command in the cut. Two such spans naming two different commands settle nothing: the author named more than one and which covers the Plan is the question

question.instructions: `plan` is the `## Plan` of a unit of work about to be started. Each option but `noMatch` is a scenario `spec/` already declares, and its description is that command's name and the comment line above it. Which scenario already covers the behaviour `plan` describes, so that writing a new one for this Plan would duplicate it?

criteria.noMatch: no scenario covers this Plan: the behaviour it describes is exercised by none of them, or the Plan changes nothing `spec/` models -- a document, a script, a measurement, a reading -- and no scenario could cover it. NOT this option: a scenario that covers the Plan's behaviour under a different name.

bands.labelled_by: THE JOIN THIS ENTRY DECLARES, RUN over each real closing diff -- never a rule re-derived beside the corpus, which is what the first build did and which disagreed with the join two ways (REVIEW at 228dd87, defect 1). The 24 negatives are the exception and say so in the case: their truth is true BY CONSTRUCTION, one edit having removed the covering command from the field. NOTHING IN THE TREE HOLDS THAT: the builder is git-ignored scratch under `runtime/`, as every builder here is, and the suite can only refuse a row naming another entry's join. Moving a builder into the tree is the fix and is not made here.
bands.why: UNCUT, AND NOT BECAUSE THE PASS WAS A FIRST ONE. The reading was measured over three runs and it does not separate: no option of it is a flag, so no cut is proposed and the entry declares none. It stays at `shadow`, where `branch` records the option and judges nothing.
bands.how: 36 states over 3 runs, sdlc-alloy#458 S7. EVERY LABEL IS THE DECLARED JOIN'S, run over the real closing diff: 8 positives -- a sub-issue whose closing pull request's `# witnesses:` line names a command already declared before it -- against 28 negatives. 4 of those are the join's own `noMatch`, a diff witnessing only commands it added itself; the other 24 are made BY ONE EDIT, 12 `sibling` (the same Plan against the largest entity holding none of the covering commands) and 12 `minus` (its own field with them removed). THE READING ANSWERS `noMatch` FOR ALMOST EVERYTHING: 28 of 28 negatives AND 7 of 8 positives, identically in all three runs. So the cut that flags every negative is 0.41-0.46 and it takes 7 of the 8 positives with it -- everything is flagged, which is not a reading. P(noMatch) AUC 0.60-0.63, AND A TOKEN-OVERLAP BASELINE OVER THE SAME LABELS BEATS IT AT 0.703 -- picking the option that shares most of the Plan's word tokens and flagging one minus that share separates these classes better than the model does. (0.59 was this baseline under the labels the corpus shipped with before the join relabelled it; both sides of a comparison have to be re-derived together, and only one was -- REVIEW at edf5ba2, defect 1.) AND IT HAS NO ADVANTAGE LEFT ON THE DISCRETE PICK EITHER: it hit the command the later diff names 0 of 8, as the baseline does. The 1 of 8 this entry claimed was `ask.py`'s `hit` field, computed against the labels of the run it was made in and never re-derived when the join relabelled the corpus -- the one pick it counted, `s61` on sdlc-alloy#442, is a command the closing diff ADDED, which the join rules out. SAME MISTAKE AS THE BASELINE ONE ABOVE, one round later: a relabelling moves every number read off the old labels, not the one you remember (REVIEW at 6b19bb5). One call a state, 1.03 measured, since the cover call is reached once.
bands.not_the_field_and_not_the_text: TWO HYPOTHESES FOR THE FAILURE WERE PROBED AND BOTH DIED. 10 states whose witnessed commands sit in ONE entity were asked again cut to THAT entity -- 18 to 159 options, the right answer certainly on offer. SORTED BY THE JOIN'S LABELS they are 6 positives and 4 negatives, not 10 positives. (1) The field is too wide -- 244 at the measurement: selection hit 0 of the 6, and the 4 negatives were answered `noMatch` 4 of 4. (2) The option text is a command name plus a group heading two words long that several commands share: the same 10 asked with the doc comment above the PRED instead, where the behaviour is written, hit 0 of the 6 and answered 3 of the 4. (Both hits read 1 before the stale `hit` field was re-derived; the pick they counted is the added command named above.) Neither moved it. What fails is the question, not its packaging.
bands.known_wrong: THE TRUTH IS A PROXY AND A WEAK ONE. A `# witnesses:` line says which scenario the work ended up TIED to, never that the scenario already covered the Plan -- and this history barely separates the two: of the 12 sub-issues that add such a line, 8 witness a command that was in the snapshot at the closing pull request's base and 4 witness only commands their own work created -- and the join labels those 4 `noMatch`, which is why the positive class is 8 and not 12. The 8 are not clean either, since a sub-issue's earlier pull request may have added the command the closing one witnesses. AND THE POPULATION IS THIN FOR A DEEPER REASON: 57 of the 69 closed sub-issues with a Plan and one closing pull request add no `# witnesses:` line at all, so nothing in this tree's history records a Plan that a pre-existing scenario covered. The duplicate this reading hunts may simply not have happened here.

state.intent: the `## Intent` section of the `kind:maintenance` sub-issue the claim names, its non-blank lines
state.hunk: one hunk of the branch's patch of a file the commit touched: `path`, and `text`, the hunk from its `@@` line, cut from `git diff` from the merge-base with origin/main to the commit

prefilter.what: a commit on a claim whose sub-issue carries `kind:maintenance`, pushed to a GitHub remote; any other claim asks nothing and logs nothing. Three hunks are settled `form_only` by code and logged as settled rows naming which rule took them: a hunk of a test suite (check-diff-screen's `TEST`); a hunk of a shell, YAML, TOML or JavaScript file whose every changed non-blank line is a comment in that language -- never prose, a `.als` or a `.py`, where a comment is the rule or the AST rule reads it; and a hunk of a `.py` file whose AST, function and class docstrings blanked, is the same before and after that hunk alone -- the module's docstring is kept, since a script prints it as its usage. A merge commit asks nothing; a file whose branch patch is empty, a binary, a failed `git diff`, a patch over check-diff-screen's ceiling, no merge-base, a commit that does not resolve, a sub-issue that would not read, one with an empty or no `## Intent`, and a reading that raised each log a skip.

question.instructions: `intent` says what a tidy-up is for. `hunk` is one change it made. Which of these is `hunk`?

form_only.what: a change of form: wording, layout, names, comments or where something lives; every input gives the same result and every rule says the same thing
form_only.example: a copied `def section(text)` replaced by an import of the identical function

asked_behaviour.what: a change of behaviour that `intent` asks for: a result or a rule differs, and `intent` names that difference
asked_behaviour.example: intent 'cap titles at 40 characters'; hunk changes `TITLE_CEILING = 60` to `TITLE_CEILING = 40`

unasked_behaviour.what: a change of behaviour that `intent` does not ask for: a result or a rule differs, and nothing in `intent` names that difference
unasked_behaviour.example: intent 'trim AGENTS.md to what filing does not own'; hunk rewrites 'a hook is never bypassed' as 'a hook is not bypassed without a reason'

unclear.what: the hunk alone cannot show whether anything runs differently: it calls or moves something whose body is not in the hunk

form-behaviour.join_why: the named fact labels almost nothing. DECISION 5726150089 names a later REVIEW finding on the hunk's file, or a later fix commit on its lines; over the 34 merged pull requests of the 25 `kind:maintenance` sub-issues, 112 of 1121 hunks carry either, and of the 46 findings behind them 3 to 5 name a behaviour change at all -- the rest are wording, a missing test or a stale citation. check-diff-screen's fact is the same fact and has the same gap. A hand label per hunk is the truth here, which is what the corpus holds

bands.cases: 144 real hunks of merged maintenance pull requests labelled by hand (60 asked_behaviour, 38 form_only, 18 unasked_behaviour, 28 unclear and unscored), 60 made by moving a hunk under a sibling sub-issue's Intent, 15 made by one behaviour edit inside a form-only hunk: 93 negatives (unasked or made) and 98 positives (form_only or asked)
bands.how: NO BAND: FEW CASES, LONG SHADOW. NO CUT IS DECLARED, so the word is the option the model picked; the flag reads P(unasked_behaviour), which the reader writes as the row's `flag`. AUC 0.80 over all (real 0.85, sibling 0.85, one edit 0.55), but the cut that flags every negative is 0.00, so it flags 98 of 98 positives too. Measured beside it on the same states: a form_only/changes_behaviour/unclear choice read on P(changes_behaviour), AUC 0.74 and 98/98 at the all-negatives cut; a noul 'does hunk change what anything does' AUC 0.61 (one edit 0.31); a noul 'does intent ask for it' read as 1-P, AUC 0.82 and 97/98; the two nouls combined 0.78 and 89/98; token overlap of intent and hunk 0.66 and 96/98; changed-line count 0.56. The paired rise of P(unasked) from a hunk to its made negative is 50 of 60 under a sibling Intent but 11 of 15 for one edit: it reads whether the Intent names the change, not whether behaviour changed. Repeat of 30 states with the store off: at most 0.08-0.11 apart, 2 word flips. Calls: 479 over 230 distinct states, 2.1 a state for the measurement (every alternative re-asked each state); the reader sends 1 a hunk. It orders and does not filter, so this stays at shadow collecting cases (sdlc-alloy#458 C2).
